name: Question 19
problem:
For the functions $p(x)$ and $q(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
p(10)=-1,\,{p}^{′}(10)=-2,\,q(10)=2,\,{q}^{′}(10)=1
$$

If $z(x)=(2p(x)+q(x))(2-p(x))$, compute ${z}^{′}(10).$
worked_solution:
The product rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(uv)=u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=2p(x)+q(x)$ and $v=2-p(x).$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2{p}^{′}(x)+{q}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=-{p}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}(x) & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(2p(x)+q(x))(-{p}^{′}(x))+(2-p(x))(2{p}^{′}(x)+{q}^{′}(x)) \\  & =-{p}^{′}(x)(2p(x)+q(x))+(2{p}^{′}(x)+{q}^{′}(x))(2-p(x)).\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=10,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}(10) & =-{p}^{′}(10)(2p(10)+q(10))+(2{p}^{′}(10)+{q}^{′}(10))(2-p(10)) \\  & =-(-2)(2(-1)+2)+(2(-2)+1)(2-(-1)) \\  & =2(-2+2)-3(2+1) \\  & =0-9 \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The product rule states that ddx(uv)=udvdx+vdudx.

Let u=2p(x)+q(x) and v=2−p(x). Differentiating each, we get dudx=2p′(x)+q′(x)anddvdx=−p′(x).

Substituting this into the product rule gives

z′(x)=udvdx+vdudx=(2p(x)+q(x))(−p′(x))+(2−p(x))(2p′(x)+q′(x))=−p′(x)(2p(x)+q(x))+(2p′(x)+q′(x))(2−p(x)).

At x=10, this gives

z′(10)=−p′(10)(2p(10)+q(10))+(2p′(10)+q′(10))(2−p(10))=−(−2)(2(−1)+2)+(2(−2)+1)(2−(−1))=2(−2+2)−3(2+1)=0−9=−9.
